correctness.rationale: Every factorial factor in a stratum must lie below the next prime. For largest prime at most 11, all possible composite indices are exhausted by six verified identities, reducing the monoid to prime-index factorials. The prime-valuation matrix is triangular with unit diagonal, so coordinates are unique. Weighted-simplex lattice counting gives the asymptotic. The 14! coordinate vector is computed in the same unimodular basis and has two negative entries, proving nonmembership in the nonnegative prime-factorial monoid.

Luca’s factorial-factorization problem is structurally different: its subject is the index of a single factorial that admits a smaller-factorial decomposition.
